section_summary: This section closes a report with a list of leftist organizations and a bibliography, then records U.S. assessments of Japanese Communist Party statements, strategy, recruitment, and influence in labor and professional groups. It includes a translated party strategy document and a revised military intelligence index of leftist organizations. The section ends with a despatch discussing General MacArthur’s July 1949 statement on communism in Japan.

subfiles.title: Report on leftist organizations in Japan: appendix and bibliography
subfiles.about: Lists organizations by degree of Communist influence and cites sources used in the preceding report.
subfiles.summary: The concluding appendix assigns grades A through E to Japanese labor, cultural, student, Korean, and other organizations according to assessed Communist influence. A bibliography lists earlier despatches, memoranda, and occupation intelligence summaries.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party Statement Regarding War
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Reports Tokuda’s statement on war and transmits a labor group’s challenge to the party.
subfiles.summary: Reports Tokuda’s pledge to resist any invader and encloses a labor group’s demand for clarity about a Soviet attack.

subfiles.title: Open Letter to the Japanese Communist Party
subfiles.from: Democratization League, National Congress of Industrial Unions
subfiles.about: Demands a clear statement of the party’s position if the Soviet Union attacks Japan.
subfiles.summary: The league argues that Japanese Communist rhetoric implies support for Soviet interests. It challenges Tokuda to say explicitly whether the party would resist a Soviet attack on Japan.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of information on Sakata Shōichi
subfiles.about: Forwards intelligence on physicist Sakata Shōichi and addresses reports that he may visit the United States.
subfiles.summary: Forwards a profile of Sakata; finds no evidence of a planned U.S. visit or direct Communist Party membership.

subfiles.title: Summary of Information: Sakata Shōichi
subfiles.from: Intelligence Division, Department of the Army
subfiles.about: Profiles Sakata’s scientific career and assesses his associations with Communist-influenced organizations.
subfiles.summary: Details Sakata’s education, research, publications, and work with Yukawa Hideki. It describes his leadership in the Nagoya branch of the Democratic Scientists’ Association while reporting that he repeatedly declined invitations to join the Communist Party.

subfiles.title: Request for lists of Japanese Communists
subfiles.about: Requests current rosters and biographical information on Japanese Communists and sympathizers.
subfiles.summary: Requests police-derived Communist lists and updated biographical records for current and potential party leaders.

subfiles.title: New Struggle Principles of Japan Communist Party
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits and interprets the Communist Political Bureau’s published struggle principles.
subfiles.summary: Sebald reads the principles as a renewed effort to build a popular front against the Yoshida government. He highlights attacks on economic recovery policies and argues that the party has adopted more openly revolutionary language, while cautioning that this does not necessarily signal imminent violence.

subfiles.title: Communist Political Bureau Bares Struggle Principles
subfiles.doc_type: translated newspaper article and party directive
subfiles.about: Sets out a campaign to unite social groups in opposition to the Yoshida government.
subfiles.summary: The directive portrays the Yoshida government as serving monopoly and foreign capital and calls for coordinated struggles over employment, wages, taxes, land, public services, and civil rights. It urges a broad united front, mass political pressure, stronger party publications, and practical Marxist-Leninist education for members.

subfiles.title: Japan Communist Party May Day Manifesto
subfiles.about: Summarizes the party’s May Day manifesto and expected demonstrations.
subfiles.summary: The airgram says the manifesto follows the party’s struggle principles, promotes a united front, and attacks the Yoshida government. It anticipates large May Day demonstrations.

subfiles.title: Index of Leftist Organizations in Japan
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits copies of a revised military intelligence index of Japanese leftist organizations.
subfiles.summary: Transmits eight copies of the revised index, including English and romanized Japanese organization names.

subfiles.title: Alphabetical Index of Leftist Organizations in Japan, Revised May 1949
subfiles.from: Civil Intelligence Section, General Headquarters, Far East Command
subfiles.about: Catalogues Japanese leftist organizations, their activities, and estimated Communist influence.
subfiles.summary: The report revises an earlier index, adding active organizations and removing dissolved or inactive ones. Its English-language roster describes labor unions, cultural societies, Korean groups, student groups, and other organizations, assigning each an A–E grade for Communist influence. A second index matches romanized Japanese names to English translations and notes that organizational names and membership change frequently.

subfiles.title: Some Recent Communist Developments in Japan
subfiles.about: Reviews Communist recruitment, propaganda, tax campaigning, organizational infiltration, and membership figures.
subfiles.summary: The memorandum reports defections from Social Democratic groups, a Communist children’s publication, and a national tax reduction campaign. It describes party activity among finance workers, medical professionals, and seamen, then presents occupational and age figures for members and recruits. Its author infers that the party is concentrating on workers likely to supply future leaders.

subfiles.title: Incoming airgram record sheet
subfiles.about: Records receipt and routing information for an incoming airgram.
subfiles.summary: Mostly blank routing sheet with a June 1949 file reference.

subfiles.title: General MacArthur’s Fourth of July Statement
subfiles.from: Cloyce K. Huston, Chargé d’Affaires ad interim
subfiles.about: Transmits MacArthur’s Independence Day statement and discusses Japanese responses to its criticism of communism.
subfiles.summary: Huston summarizes MacArthur’s argument that American democratic ideas have taken hold in Japan and resisted Communist appeals. He notes that MacArthur’s question about legal protection for Communists may strengthen calls to outlaw the Japan Communist Party, and reviews early newspaper reactions. The listed enclosure falls beyond this section.
